notes: One portrait is now enough to build a face-LoRA training set. The character editor's new Expand set with Grok takes the first selfie reference and has Grok Imagine's edit model — hosted on fal, so the existing key and browser path just work, about two cents an image — re-shoot the same person twelve ways: three-quarter views from both sides, a profile, above and below angles, waist-up and full-body framing, laughing and neutral expressions, window daylight, lamp light, golden hour, flat overcast, harsh night flash, moody shadow, and a candid cafe look. Results land in a review grid as they finish; identity drifts sometimes, so everything starts kept and one tap drops an impostor before Add puts the survivors into the reference row. The reference cap rises from 10 to 20 to hold the expanded set, since a varied 15–20 images trains a visibly better likeness than a handful of similar shots — then Train face LoRA bakes them in as before. Closing the sheet stops further generations, failures are logged per shot without sinking the batch, and the endpoint's parameter shape is probed once and adapted to automatically.
